newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks end up on busier day.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks end up on busier day.

text.p: The Australian share market gained one percent in steady trade on Wednesday after the Dow gained two percent on Tuesday following weaker than expected March U.S. CPI data.
The key share barometer, the All Ordinaries index ended up 24.7 points at 2,406.4, near its intra-day high of 2,410.7.
The June share price index closed up 39 points at 2,402 and at a 4.4 point discount to the underlying index.
Investors targeted a range of blue chip issues with market heavyweights, Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd and National Australia Bank Ltd, the most active issues.

"It was pretty buoyant across the board after the Dow's rise but I think shares were also helped by the strong local bond market," said Derek Bond, a senior dealer at Brisbane brokerage, Burrell & Co.
"Investors were mainly chasing the quality end of the market," Bond said.
Bond said Lend Lease Corp Ltd's 54 cent gain to A$22.32 (US$17.19) and Brambles Industries Ltd's 54 cent climb to A$22.32 was indicative of the market's appetite for quality issues on the day.
Other outstanding issues included Papua New Guinea gold miner Lihir Gold Ltd whose stock rose on solid turnover with a number of large parcels put through the market by Brisbane broker Wilson HTM.
The shares of retailer Woolworths Ltd rose 12 cents to A$3.82 on volume of 10.6 million shares as the market factored in the group's continued solid sales growth.
